newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana president dumps deputy in re-election bid.
newsitem.headline: Ghana president dumps deputy in re-election bid.

text.p: Ghana's President Jerry Rawlings filed his nomination papers on Tuesday for presidential elections on December 7 but dumped his vice-president from the ticket.
Rawlings, seeking a second and final four-year mandate, chose income tax chief and former school mate James Atta Mills as his running mate, dropping Vice-President Kow Arkaah.
Arkaah was previously allied with Rawlings but increasing antagonism between them exploded into a much publicised scuffle during a cabinet meeting last December.

Arkaah has taken his National Convention Party out of an alliance with the ruling National Democratic Congress. His party has joined forces with the opposition New Patriotic Party and the Peoples Convention Party in the "Great Alliance".
He has already been picked as running mate of Alliance candidate John Agyekum Kufuor, who also filed his papers with the Electoral Commission on Tuesday.
Four other candidates have yet to register their nominations for the poll, to be held simultaneously with legislative elections.
The presidential vote is organised along U.S. lines with candidates for the presidency and vice-presidency running together.
Rawlings is a former air force flight lieutenant who staged two successful coups before turning politician.
Opposition parties boycotted the 1992 parliamentary polls after accusing Rawlings of manipulating the presidential vote.
